evals.name: black-canvas-debug
evals.prompt: My WebGL2 fragment shader compiles fine — `getShaderInfoLog` returns nothing — but the canvas is just black. Walk me through the most likely causes and how to diagnose each one without throwing more code at it.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis checklist that covers the canonical black-canvas causes (forgot clear, viewport not set after resize, wrong VAO bound, attribute not enabled, uniform set on wrong program, depth test culling, bound program ≠ used program) with a way to narrow down each.
expectations: Distinguishes shader compile from program link (recommends checking `getProgramInfoLog`, not just shader log)
Identifies viewport-after-resize as a likely culprit
Recommends checking the bound program and VAO at draw time
Recommends Spector.js (or equivalent capture tool)
Mentions depth test as a possible suspect
Mentions face culling as a possible suspect
Mentions uniform-set-on-wrong-program as a possible suspect
Answers as an ordered diagnostic checklist rather than dumping rewritten code
First 3 diagnostic steps focus on highest-yield checks (link status, viewport, bound program/VAO) rather than rare causes
Each diagnostic step includes a concrete API call or inspection command, not vague 'check your X' advice
Honors the 'no more code' framing — recommends inspection/diagnosis over rewriting

evals.name: mouse-circle-shader
evals.prompt: Write me a minimal raw WebGL2 fragment shader (no framework) that fills a 600x600 canvas with a soft white-on-black circle that follows the mouse position. Include the host HTML/JS to pipe in `u_resolution` and `u_mouse` uniforms.
evals.expected_output: A single HTML file with a vertex shader (fullscreen quad), fragment shader using `smoothstep` for the soft edge, uniform setup for resolution + mouse, mouse event listener that updates the uniform (with y-flip if needed), and a render loop.
expectations: Output is a single self-contained HTML file with no external assets
Uses WebGL2 (`#version 300 es` shader directive)
Uses `smoothstep` to create the soft edge
Declares uniforms named exactly `u_resolution` and `u_mouse`
Flips mouse Y coordinate to match `gl_FragCoord` (bottom-origin)
Sets the canvas backing-store size with `devicePixelRatio` for HiDPI sharpness
Checks shader compile and program link errors (throws or logs on failure)
HTML is runnable from `file://` with no build step
Initial mouse state is seeded (e.g., to canvas center) so the circle is visible on first frame before mouse movement
Mouse-to-canvas math uses `getBoundingClientRect()` so it works if the canvas has CSS margins/padding

evals.name: instanced-rendering
evals.prompt: I want to render 10,000 instances of the same small mesh in raw WebGL2 — no Three.js, no other framework. What's the right approach and what are the pitfalls? Show me the key API calls.
evals.expected_output: Recommends `drawArraysInstanced` / `drawElementsInstanced` + per-instance attributes via `vertexAttribDivisor`. Mentions VAO setup, per-instance data layout (model matrix or position+color), and pitfalls like divisor staying set across VAOs or forgetting to enable per-instance attributes.
expectations: Recommends `drawArraysInstanced` or `drawElementsInstanced` (single draw call)
Mentions `vertexAttribDivisor(loc, 1)` for per-instance attributes
Provides concrete code for the per-instance attribute setup
Mentions the `mat4`-attribute-takes-4-slots pitfall
Notes that divisor state is part of the VAO (or otherwise warns about VAO state)
Mentions either WebGL1 fallback (`ANGLE_instanced_arrays`) or `gl_InstanceID`
Mentions caching attribute/uniform locations (not querying per frame)
Provides a verification or diagnostic section for instancing-specific symptoms
Mentions `STREAM_DRAW` / `bufferSubData` (or equivalent) for per-frame-updated instance data
If `gl_InstanceID` is mentioned, notes that it is an `int` (cast to `float` before arithmetic, or use it in integer contexts only)

evals.name: rotating-textured-cube
evals.prompt: Set up a minimal WebGL2 page that renders a rotating textured cube with no framework. I want to actually understand each step — buffers, shaders, matrices, texture loading, draw loop. Make it one self-contained HTML file.
evals.expected_output: Single HTML file with: cube vertex+UV+index data in VBOs, vertex shader applying model-view-projection, fragment shader sampling a texture, texture loaded from an image or DataURL, perspective projection matrix, animation loop rotating the model matrix each frame, proper resize handling, and a clear render.
expectations: Single self-contained HTML file with no external assets (procedural or inline texture)
Cube uses 24 vertices (4 per face) so each face has its own UVs
Uses indexed drawing (`drawElements`)
Enables `DEPTH_TEST` and clears `DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT` each frame
Uses WebGL2 (`#version 300 es`)
Updates `gl.viewport` whenever the canvas is resized
Checks shader compile and program link errors
Explanation walks through buffers, shaders, matrices, texture loading, and the draw loop
Passes `false` to the `transpose` flag of `uniformMatrix4fv` (the only legal value in WebGL)
Composes model × view × projection from a working 4x4 matrix helper or library
Sets `gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL, true)` before `texImage2D` (or flips V in shader) so the texture isn't upside down
Enables `CULL_FACE` and sets `cullFace(BACK)` + `frontFace(CCW)` consistent with the cube's vertex winding
Caches uniform locations once after link rather than re-querying per frame
